drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our proposed revisions to the mutual NDA. We have clarified the confidentiality and permitted-use obligations, added customary exclusions and compelled-disclosure procedures, and addressed return or destruction of information and survival. These provisions are mutual. Please confirm the parties’ full legal names and advise on your preferred governing law and forum.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the “Purpose”). “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed by or on behalf of either party to the other in connection with the Purpose, in any form, including analyses derived from that information and the existence, status and terms of the parties’ discussions. Neither party is obligated to disclose information or proceed with any transaction, and no transaction commitment arises unless a definitive agreement is executed.

2. CONFIDENTIALITY AND PERMITTED USE. Each receiving party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it with at least reasonable care and no less than the care it uses for its own similarly sensitive information. Disclosure is permitted only to its personnel and professional advisers who need to know for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement or applicable professional duties. The receiving party is responsible for their breaches of this Agreement. Confidential Information excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate is publicly available without breach, was lawfully known without restriction before disclosure, is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of Confidential Information. If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt prior notice, reasonably cooperate at the disclosing party’s expense in seeking protection, and disclose only what is legally required. Upon written request, the receiving party shall return or destroy Confidential Information, except copies required by law, professional retention obligations or routine automated backups; retained information remains subject to this Agreement and may not be used for any other purpose.

3. TERM AND SURVIVAL. This Agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and remains in effect for twenty-four months. Confidentiality and permitted-use obligations survive for three years following termination or expiration; for information constituting a trade secret, those obligations continue for so long as that information remains a trade secret under applicable law.

4. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which damages may be inadequate. Either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief, subject to applicable law, in addition to any other available remedies.

We also propose five years’ survival for ordinary Confidential Information, retaining the trade-secret protection as drafted; full legal names and governing law/forum remain subject to client confirmation.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the “Purpose”). “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information disclosed by or on behalf of either party to the other in connection with the Purpose, whether before, on or after the effective date of this Agreement, in any form, including analyses derived from that information and the existence, status and terms of the parties’ discussions. Neither party is obligated to disclose information or proceed with any transaction, and no transaction commitment arises unless a definitive agreement is executed.

2. CONFIDENTIALITY AND PERMITTED USE. Each receiving party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it with at least reasonable care and no less than the care it uses for its own similarly sensitive information. Disclosure is permitted only to its personnel and professional advisers who need to know for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement or applicable professional duties. The receiving party is responsible for their breaches of this Agreement. Confidential Information excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate is publicly available without breach, was lawfully known without restriction before disclosure, is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of Confidential Information. If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt prior notice, reasonably cooperate at the disclosing party’s expense in seeking protection, and disclose only what is legally required. Upon becoming aware of any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information, the receiving party shall promptly notify the disclosing party and take reasonable steps to stop the unauthorized use or disclosure, mitigate its effects and prevent its recurrence. Within 30 days after the disclosing party’s written request, the receiving party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information, including copies held by its personnel and professional advisers, and provide written certification of compliance by an authorized representative. The receiving party and its personnel and professional advisers may retain only copies required by applicable law and copies in automated backup systems that are inaccessible in the ordinary course of business. The certification shall identify any applicable retention exception. Retained copies shall remain subject to this Agreement’s confidentiality and permitted-use protections for as long as retained and shall not be accessed or used except as legally required or as necessary for backup restoration, in which case restored copies shall promptly be returned or destroyed unless retention is legally required.

3. TERM AND SURVIVAL. This Agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and remains in effect for twenty-four months. Confidentiality and permitted-use obligations survive for five years following termination or expiration; for information constituting a trade secret, those obligations continue for so long as that information remains a trade secret under applicable law. The continuing protections for retained copies under Section 2 are not limited by the foregoing survival periods.
Full legal names of both parties remain subject to client confirmation.
Governing law and forum remain open pending client confirmation; no selection is made in this draft.
